solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A wife has to reach round a table for him and his comrades?

definitions.text: a table for him and his comrades?
definitions.note: the Round Table of King Arthur, where his knights sat together

indicators.note: the verb reach is placed round the earlier pieces, so it encloses them

parts.note: to reach a place or goal is to gain it

explanation.surface: A married woman must stretch across the dinner table to serve a man and his friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' does double duty in the surface: it is the container signal and also suggests the Round Table, so the definition leans on the word before it, as the blogger noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain was one of the Arthurian knights who sat at the Round Table with his fellow knights.

clue.text: Painter's sign almost not complete

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nary, a dialect word for not one, as in nary a word
to do a job is to complete it

explanation.surface: An artist's signature is almost unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Painter is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance artist who produced the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Two little beasts raised another

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a kid is a young goat, a little beast, and two of them side by side

explanation.surface: A pair of young animals brought up a third one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another little beast: the dik-dik is a tiny antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The dik-dik is a small African antelope, so it is another little creature after the two young goats.

clue.text: We might prosecute Crimean War with silly bastard

indicators.note: bastard as an adjective means debased or irregular, so the letters are misshapen into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone insults an idiotic person for bringing up the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawyers practising in the criminal courts are the ones who conduct prosecutions of offenders.

clue.text: Finally blowing smoke over my dish

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written, its closing letter only
reek is an old and Scottish word for smoke
my! and God! are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A cook blowing smoke across their plate of food at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is informal for an attractive person, not a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: An exceptionally handsome man is called both a dish and an Adonis-like figure from Olympus.

clue.text: Informally, very much corruption after tax returns

definitions.note: used as an adverb, as in spoiled rotten, meaning extremely

parts.note: rot is decay or moral corruption

indicators.note: returns means the phrase's synonym is read backwards

parts.note: pay after tax is net pay

explanation.surface: Corruption follows on the heels of a tax return, very much so.
explanation.definitionFit: In colloquial use the adverb, as in spoilt rotten, means to an extreme degree.

clue.text: Stone mostly cut to break diamond, say, right away

indicators.note: the cut piece breaks into the other word, splitting it open
right away means R, the abbreviation for right, is removed

parts.note: diamond is a form of the element carbon

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: A gem is cut to split a diamond, then taken away at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamond, say' signals an example: diamond is one form of the element, so the definition by example is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabochon is a gemstone polished into a smooth dome rather than cut with facets.

clue.text: Workshop canteen regularly visited by one down?

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: a lier is one who lies down

explanation.surface: A works canteen is periodically checked by an inspector?
explanation.walkthrough: 'one down?' is not a cross-reference to another clue: it means someone lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a place where creative work is made.

clue.text: Hotel managed to get round variable fne

indicators.note: the first word is placed around the following pieces

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
Y is a conventional letter for a variable in algebra
the blog's text drops the fi of fine; OK means fine

explanation.surface: A hotel operated in order to get round a variable fine.
explanation.definitionFit: A ryokan is a traditional Japanese inn where guests sleep on tatami mats.

clue.text: Girl, perhaps asleep, gets expelled

annotationWithheld.why: Girl, perhaps asleep, gets expelled (6): ANN inside BED, where asleep (in bed) gives BED and is also the container signal, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: First signs of an electric storm damaged good conductor

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so the letters are put in a new order
first signs takes the opening letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: The opening flashes of an electric storm damaged a good conductor of lightning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good conductor' reads like a lightning rod in a storm, but it is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished leader of an orchestra, a master of the baton.

clue.text: One-piece exotic robe worn by king embraced by wayward nun

indicators.note: the inner pieces are held inside the scrambled word
wayward means wandering off course, so the letters are rearranged
a robe worn by someone goes around them, so the king goes inside
exotic means strange or unusual, signalling the letters are rearranged

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: An outlandish garment worn by a monarch is hugged by a misbehaving nun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-piece' looks like a swimsuit word from the robe picture, but it means whole, not split.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whole and undivided, made in a single piece, has not been split.

clue.text: Leader once grand, also not half tall

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, G for short
and means also, in addition

indicators.note: not half keeps only one half of the word

parts.note: tall means high

explanation.surface: A former chief was once grand and not half tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Coming back to strengthen repaired container with hard core? Good

indicators.note: the synonym for hard goes into the core of the rearranged word
something repaired is put back together, here in a new letter order

parts.note: hard means solid

explanation.surface: A mended box with a hard centre returns to strengthen things, good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming back' is part of the definition: the prefix re- means again, so the strengthening happens a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsolidate is to make firm again, strengthening something once more.

clue.text: Inequity — unstable or stable property?

definitions.note: a playful reading: the quality of things found in a stable, that is horses

indicators.note: unstable means not settled, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Is unfairness shaky, or is it a firm asset?
explanation.walkthrough: 'stable' looks like an adjective meaning firm; here it is where horses are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A coined word for horsiness, the equine quality of animals that live in a stable.

clue.text: In one month, caught radical showing sign of authority?

indicators.note: in means the following letter goes inside the month

parts.note: Sept is the abbreviation for September
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a red is a political radical

explanation.surface: Within a month a revolutionary was arrested, revealing a symbol of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding a royal staff, the emblem of a monarch's power, as in Shakespeare's sceptred isle.

clue.text: After a short time, those discharged honourably reported audacity

indicators.note: after puts the following piece behind the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: reported means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: emeriti are those retired with honour, keeping their title

explanation.surface: Soon afterwards, honourably retired veterans were said to show boldness.
explanation.walkthrough: Emeriti, plural of emeritus, are professors retired with honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is rash boldness, the nerve to do something reckless.

clue.text: After getting let off, ebullient crook is ft for match

definitions.note: the blog's text drops the fi of fit; old-fashioned use for a young woman ready to marry

indicators.note: crook is Australian slang for unwell or faulty, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Once released, a crooked yet bubbly person is fit to play in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After getting let off' reads as a release from custody, but it tells you to take three letters away before the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubile traditionally describes a young woman of an age suitable for marriage.

clue.text: Girl entering the answers?

parts.note: something entering a place is in it
a crossword's answers go into the grid

explanation.surface: A young woman writing her answers into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's given name, as in the actress Ingrid Bergman.

clue.text: Unreasonable habit-cum-bent

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A nun's garment and a crooked fellow, which seems excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit much means it is excessive or unfair.

clue.text: Challenge male boxer when breaking in

indicators.note: the pieces break into the word in, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written
a pug is a slang word for a pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A man contests a fighter when he breaks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn a claim is to dispute or call it into question.

clue.text: Shark with one on board

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with
a man is a piece in board games such as chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A shark swimming with a sailor aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A shark is a swindler, someone who cheats people out of money.

clue.text: Almost having time to get locked up late in the day?

indicators.note: the time letter is shut inside the other word

parts.note: nighly is an old word meaning almost or nearly

explanation.surface: Nearly having to be locked up until late in the day?
explanation.walkthrough: NIGHLY is an archaic adverb for almost, from nigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens every evening happens late in the day, with a question mark for the stretch.

clue.text: Rear engineers stopping to gasp for breath

indicators.note: the engineers plug the middle of the word, like a stopper

parts.note: to pant is to gasp for air
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers at the back stop to catch their breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like a noun meaning the back, but it is the verb meaning bring up children.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear a child is to raise it, as a mother or father does.

clue.text: One wouldn't work on this

parts.note: industrial action in which workers down tools

explanation.definitionFit: A walkout by employees, the occasion when they refuse to do their jobs.

clue.text: Meeting Watergate suspect after cover's blown

indicators.note: suspect means dubious, signalling the letters are not in their proper order
with its cover gone the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A gathering following the Watergate scandal, the cover-up exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: WATERGATE loses its first and last letters to give ATERGAT, which is rearranged. Watergate was the 1970s US political scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a meet of boat races, a sporting event on water.
